newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia pipeline blast, pumping to restart soon.
newsitem.headline: Colombia pipeline blast, pumping to restart soon.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp said it hoped to start pumping crude along Colombia's largest pipeline again by late Thursday or early Friday after a dynamite attack by leftist rebels.

Suspected National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas blasted the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline for the 35th time this year Wednesday, a company spokesman said. No estimate was available on the amount of crude spilled.

Occidental's corporate relations manager Robert Stewart said that a spate of five rebel attacks in less than one month had forced a cut in production from 180,000 barrels per day to an average of 171,000 barrels per day at its Cano Limon field in eastern Arauca province.
The pipeline which runs to the lifting terminal at Covenas on the Caribbean coast transports about 250,000 barrels of crude per day.

About 100,000 barrels of crude have been lost in dynamite attacks on the pipeline so far this year, generating a cost of more than $9.3 million in clean-up bills and the value of lost crude, state-run oil company Ecopetrol said.
Last year the pipeline was blown up 47 times with a loss of 105,000 barrels of crude.
